newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end sharply down on crackdown fear.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end sharply down on crackdown fear.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B shares ended sharply down on Tuesday on renewed fears that Beijing may take further measures to rein in the stock markets, traders said.
The domestic A share index ended down 35.263 points or 2.65 percent to 1,295.905 points and the foreign currency B share index lost 0.827 points or 0.96 percent to 85.321 points.

Traders said renewed market rumours predicted Beijing would shortly announce new measures to cool down stock trading, including a three-day settlement system to replace the current one-day settlement system on the domestic A share market.

"Renewed rumours greatly hurt market sentiment already weak due to a series of offical crackdown measures," said one trader. "Potential for further falls on the A share markets is still great but that for the B share markets will be limited."
Brokers said they believed the B share index would meet support at the 85-point level.
A total of 12 million B shares at value of $9.4 million were traded on Tuesday. Of 43 B shares, 35 traded, with 16 down, 10 flat and nine up.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co was the biggest loser on institutional liquidation selling, plunging $0.056 or 9.75 percent to $0.518 on volume of 618,300 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Product Co was the most actively traded on volume of 2.2 million shares, ending unchanged at $0.864 due to institutional support, traders said.
The A share market had a volume of 254.4 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed down 110.643 points or 2.80 percent to 3,846.388 points.
Shanghai Jiafeng Co was the worst performer, falling 0.56 yuan to hit a 10-percent limit-down of 5.02 yuan.
